intro: Della is an AI employee I'm building for nail salons, starting with communications and bookings but with the goal of understanding how the business works and being able to do more of the work around it.
why: I started working on Della in March of 2026 as OpenOperator. I was spending a lot of time studying the foundations of AI, and around the OpenClaw moment I began learning about agentic AI and thinking that eventually, if not already, these models and agents would get better than any human across tasks on a computer. What they wouldn't know out of the box, though, was how a particular business worked and how to use the actual systems inside it.

I started looking at medspas, but the compliance side pushed me more toward nail salons because it was a similar, adjacent business, and I thought communications were a place to start because leads often get lost there and there was something specific I could test: when someone asks for an appointment and Della checks the calendar, the appointment actually ends up in the salon's booking system.
bookingProblem: Early on, Della would sometimes say it had booked an appointment when it hadn't, which meant the caller could think they were booked in while the salon had nothing on its calendar, so I had to make the booking result part of the process instead of relying on what the model said had happened.
sources: A salon's cancellation policy can come from the information it has given Della, but when someone asks whether 4:30 is open, it has to check the current calendar because that answer can change between calls.
technical: The harness is the software I'm building around the model so it can use the salon's information and booking tools, keep customer context between conversations, and check what actually happened when it tried to do something, rather than treating the model's response as proof that the work was done.
memory: During one of my test calls I told Della that I had chipped my nail, and when I called again a couple of days later it asked how my nail was doing and whether I had gone to the doctor for it.
That was cool because it wasn't starting over from zero and was able to remember something from my last conversation and bring it back up on the next call.
control: I don't want the owner to have to approve every normal booking, but I also don't want Della making decisions they never agreed to, so the owner chooses what it can handle on its own and what has to come back to them.
messages: Calls were where I started, but I don't want Della to just be a receptionist, so I'm expanding into messages and follow-up with the same customer context behind them, rather than having every conversation start over depending on how someone reaches the salon.
latency: All of those checks and lookups take time, which matters a lot when someone is waiting on the phone, so I'm working on the database and memory side to keep the calls moving without skipping the information Della needs, although some of the delay still comes from the model itself.
current: I've had calls go through the system and create appointments in Square, and now I'm working on getting it into salons while improving how it handles the situations where something doesn't go through or needs a person to step in.
direction: Over time, I want Della to be able to use what happens in the salon to notice work that needs doing and follow through on it, because the point of giving it the business's information and systems is for it to be able to do more than just respond whenever someone calls.
